newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog keeps up pressure on pensions scandal.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog keeps up pressure on pensions scandal.

text.p: Britain's top financial watchdog the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) on Friday opened a new front in its campaign to help victims of pensions misselling.
The regulator called on employers and occupational pension scheme trustees to help personal pensions misselling victims.

The SIB, which last month launched an advertising campaign underlining the importance of the public playing its part in the review, published a factsheet explaining to employers and trustees "how their help is vital in putting things right".

More than half-a-million people may have been wrongly advised to take out personal pensions instead of staying with occupational schemes between 1988 and 1994 and regulators have moved to speed up compensation payments to those who lost out.
"Thousands of people are losing out on the benefits of an occupational pension scheme because they were wrongly advised to take out a personal pension instead," the SIB said in a statement.
In 1994 SIB told the pension industry to undertake a widespread review of all personal pensions sold between the end of April 1988 and the end of June 1994.
Since then firms involved in the review have been set target deadline to complete all cases by 1998.
The factsheet includes a checklist of five ways employers and trustees can help.

These include providing scheme information to reviewing firms when requested, answering one-off requests for information from employees and deciding whether to let those affected by misselling join the scheme for future service.
They can also decide whether to let employees back into the scheme for the past and take action to raise awareness of the review, SIB said.
It said the factsheet had been welcomed by the Confederation of British Industry (CBI) and the National Association of Pension Funds.
